text:
Help me write a public comment. I run a charter fishing boat out of our harbor, and the state fish and wildlife commission is taking comment on cutting the daily summer flounder limit from 4 fish per angler to 2.

Facts:
- I've run my boat for 22 years. I take out about 160 trips a season at $900 a trip for up to 6 people.
- There are 11 charter boats in our harbor.
- In a survey our charter association ran, 41 of 70 past customers said they would book fewer trips if the limit drops to 2. 12 said they'd book the same number.
- The commission staff's report says the flounder stock is at 78% of its target and recommends the cut for 3 years.
- Charter boats land about 9% of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80%.
- The last time the limit was cut, in 2016, my bookings dropped from 170 trips to 138 the next season and came back to 155 two years later.

I want to say this limit will put every charter boat in our harbor out of business. I get two minutes at the microphone.

I can help with this. One thing first: your own numbers don't back up "every boat in our harbor will go out of business." In 2016 your bookings fell about 19% and then came back to 155. The commission staff will have the 2016 data too. If you open with a claim they can disprove, they may discount the rest of your two minutes. I think the strongest case is what this cut will cost you and the harbor, in dollars and in jobs, plus a specific alternative. A few questions so I can build that:

1. **What do you want the commission to do?** Keep the limit at 4? Set it at 3? Give charter boats their own limit, since you land 9% and private boats land 80%? Shorten the cut to 1–2 years with a review? A specific request is much more likely to change a vote than a general "no."

2. **What did 2016 actually cost you, and where is your breaking point?** Losing 32 trips at $900 is about $28,800 in a season. Did that put you in the red? About how many trips a season do you need to break even? Did any boats in the harbor close, sell, or cut crew after 2016?

3. **How big is the drop in the survey?** Do you know how many fewer trips the 41 customers said they'd book? What did the other 17 say (fewer than 4 fish wouldn't matter, unsure, or something else)?

4. **What has your fleet already done for the stock?** For example, catch reporting, release practices, voluntary limits, or helping with surveys. This answers their main objection: "the stock is at 78% of target and we have to act."

5. **The details for the comment itself:** your name, boat name, harbor, whether you speak for the charter association, and the hearing date. Do the commissioners know you or your association, and is there any history there?

6. **Is there anything the commission knows or will find out that hurts your case?** For example, did the charter fleet predict ruin in 2016 too, or has the stock been falling for several years?

Answer what you can. I'll leave out anything you don't know rather than guess.

1. A 3-fish limit or a shorter season instead of going to 2. Either one we can live with.

2. I don't know my break-even number offhand, and I don't know if any boats closed or cut crew after 2016. Two other captains here have told me they'd sell if bookings drop like they did in 2016. I can only speak to my own books, not how many boats would close. But I still want the harbor point as strong as you can make it without saying something false.

3. Don't know how many fewer trips the 41 said, and don't know what the other 17 said.

4. Nothing past I can point to. But I can commit to giving commission staff my trip logs from 2016 on, and our association can commit to testing a catch-reporting app with the staff next season.

5. Captain Ray Dunn, the Sea Lark. Don't know about speaking for the association, the hearing date, or whether the commissioners know us.

6. I don't dispute the staff's stock numbers and I don't have an answer to them. Also about 70% of my trips this season are already booked.

<final_document>
Good evening, commissioners. I'm Captain Ray Dunn. I've run the charter boat Sea Lark out of our harbor for 22 years, about 160 trips a season.

I don't dispute your staff's numbers. The stock is at 78 percent of target, and it needs help. I'm here to ask you to give it that help with a 3-fish limit or a shorter season instead of cutting to 2 fish.

Here's what I know from my own books. The last time the limit was cut, in 2016, my bookings fell from 170 trips to 138 the next season. That's 32 trips, close to $29,000 at today's rates. It took two years to climb back to 155, and I never got back to 170.

This time looks worse. Our charter association surveyed 70 past customers. Forty-one said they would book fewer trips at 2 fish. Only 12 said they'd book the same.

There are 11 charter boats in our harbor. I can only speak for my own books. But two other captains have told me that if bookings fall the way they did in 2016, they'll sell. Each boat that goes takes crew jobs and customers that the docks, tackle shops and restaurants count on.

Charter boats land about 9 percent of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80. For a private angler, 2 fish means a shorter day. For us, it decides whether customers book at all.

We want to help you get the data right. I'll give your staff my trip logs from 2016 on, and our association will test a catch-reporting app with your staff next season.

Please choose a 3-fish limit or a shorter season. Either one lets the stock recover and keeps our boats running. Thank you.
</final_document>

Some notes before you use it:

- **Length:** It's about 290 words, which runs close to two minutes at a normal pace. Time yourself reading it out loud. If you need to cut, drop the private-boat comparison first.
- **The harbor point:** I kept it to what you can stand behind: what's in your books, what two captains told you, and what a lost boat means for the docks. Nothing in it claims boats will close.
- **The association commitment:** You weren't sure you can speak for the association. Before the hearing, confirm they'll back testing the reporting app. If they won't, change that line to "I'll ask our association to test…"
- **"At today's rates":** This is there because your 2016 price may not have been $900. If you know the 2016 price, you can use the actual dollar figure.
- **What I left out:** I didn't mention that 70% of your trips are already booked. A commissioner could take it as a sign that demand is fine. If someone asks, you can answer honestly: those customers booked expecting a 4-fish limit, and you don't yet know how many will keep their trips.
